title: Türgesh
capsule: The Türgesh were a Turkic tribal confederation that rose to power in Semirechye (the Ili and Chu river valleys of present-day Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan) after the collapse of Western Göktürk power in 657; the dataset attests them from 692 to 749. Under Sulu Qaghan (r. 717–738) the Türgesh were the principal Central Asian force resisting both the Tang dynasty's westward expansion and the early Umayyad push into Transoxiana, defeating Arab forces at the Battle of the Defile (Passes) in 731. Sulu's assassination by a rival faction in 738 triggered a civil war between Yellow and Black Türgesh factions; the Tang general Gao Xianzhi exploited this weakness, and by 749 the Karluk confederation had destroyed Türgesh power in Semirechye.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Türgesh territorial extent is poorly attested; it is reconstructed from Tang dynasty annals and Arabic geographic sources, with the core territory in Semirechye broadly identified but steppe frontiers highly conjectural.
